title: Attaining Fundamental Limits of Multiparameter Incoherent Optical Imaging Using Joint-Detection Quantum Measurements
authors: Nico Deshler, Aakash Warke, Michael R. Grace, Amit Ashok, Saikat Guha
abstract: Resolving extended incoherent objects below the diffraction limit poses an application-rich imaging challenge whose solution may enable a new generation of observational instruments and capabilities. In this work, we invoke a practical model for general imaging by approximating an arbitrary extended incoherent object as a finite grid of thermal point emitters parameterized by their brightnesses. We derive the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) for simultaneous brightness estimation and show that the symmetric logarithmic derivatives weakly commute, indicating that the Helstrom bound furnishes the ultimate quantum limit on the estimation error for incoherent imaging. Furthermore, for deeply sub-diffraction scenes, we find numerical evidence of a gap between the Nagaoka-Hayashi (NH) bound and the Helstrom bound. This gap reveals that separable measurements, though more experimentally accessible, are insufficient to reach the quantum limit, and points to the prospective advantage of joint measurements acting on multiple state copies. Additionally, we show that spatial mode-demultiplexing (SPADE) often saturates the NH bound solidifying its status as a near-optimal separable measurement strategy that significantly outperforms direct imaging. Finally, we articulate two joint detection receivers implemented with bona fide quantum resources that asymptotically achieve the Helstrom bound.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of super-resolution imaging by determining the ultimate quantum limit for estimating multiple incoherent light sources. It proves that while separable measurements (like SPADE) are practical, they fall short of the theoretical quantum limit set by the Helstrom bound. The authors propose and analyze joint quantum detection receivers that can asymptotically reach this fundamental quantum limit.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental quantum limits for simultaneously estimating the brightnesses of multiple, extended, incoherent point emitters below the diffraction limit.
main_result: It demonstrates that joint quantum measurements are necessary to surpass the limits of separable measurements, achieving the ultimate quantum limit set by the Helstrom bound.
method: The authors derive the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) and analyze the commutation relations of the Symmetric Logarithmic Derivatives (SLDs) to establish the ultimate estimation bound.
model_or_system: The model approximates an extended incoherent object as a finite grid of thermal point emitters, whose received state is a Gaussian state parameterized by unknown brightnesses.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM), Helstrom bound, Nagaoka-Hayashi (NH) bound, and the Mean-Squared Error (MSE).
important_parameters: The number of emitters ($K$), the degree of sub-diffraction regime ($\Delta$), and the number of state copies ($n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the pupil function is inversion-symmetric and that the state is full rank; it also compares the performance of joint vs. separable measurements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of quantum and classical bounds for 1D emitters, and show simulated reconstructions comparing adaptive SPADE measurements against direct imaging for 2D grids.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the physical model and deriving the QFIM, to comparing various estimation bounds (Helstrom vs. NH), and finally articulating two specific joint detection receivers that asymptotically achieve the Helstrom bound.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous quantum information-theoretic tools to analyze measurement limitations in quantum optics, particularly showing how joint measurements can overcome classical separability constraints in imaging.

FIG. 2. Scalar CRBs for brightness estimation under differ- ent emitter geometries involving K sources of equal bright- ness. The nearest-neighbor separation for cluster was set to w/4. The NH bound is approximately 2× greater than the Helstrom bound for all geometries considered. SPADE consistently outperforms direct imaging while saturating the single-copy NH bound under particular geometries. Condition numbers for the Gram matrices of each scene ranged between ∼101 −108 for K = 3, . . . , 20. The colored lines connect- ing each emitter encode the magnitude of the gram matrix element |Gij| measuring the overlap between spatial modes excited by the jth and kth emitter.

FIG. 3. Relative CRBs normalized by the Helstrom bound as a function of the object scale (scene dilation factor ∆) for three different emitter geometries. In the resolved regime (∆≫1) all bounds converge to the Helstrom bound indepen- dent of the emitter geometry. Here the Gram matrix is ap- proximately diagonal such that the brightness of each emitter is decoupled into orthogonal modes. When the size of the ob- ject falls below the diffraction limit (∆≪1), we see that the ratio between CRBs exceeds 1, highlighting a regime where joint detection measurements provide a genuine enhancement.
